title: Idempotency in Integration
summary: Repeating the same request does not create duplicate business effects.
explain: Networks retry. Partners resend. Without idempotency keys (e.g., orderId), retries create duplicate orders. Design receivers to detect duplicates, use natural business keys, and route poison messages to DLQ. Retries without idempotency amplify outages.
analogy: Pressing 'pay' twice should not charge twice — the cashier checks the receipt number.
whyItMatters: Duplicate business documents destroy trust faster than downtime.
mnemonic: TWICE-CLICK ONCE: Retries may fire twice; business result must happen once.
useCases: Greenfield design workshop: decide if “Idempotency in Integration” is required given constraints (latency, clean-core, team skills).
Partner retries the same order POST — Idempotency in Integration prevents double billing.
Architecture review board: defend why you accepted residual risk around “Idempotency in Integration”.
